mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP indicates strong economic demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns as corporate earnings are expected to rise.
failure_condition: GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over the next 20 days more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 6% signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as economic growth may slow.
failure_condition: Unemployment rate rises above 6% but S&P 500 returns remain positive more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment increases and employment decreases, it indicates a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Unemployment rises and employment falls, but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, higher federal funds rates increase borrowing costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Federal funds rate exceeds 4.5% but S&P 500 returns remain positive more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates strong supply activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns as economic output grows.
failure_condition: Industrial production growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over the next 60 days more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in retail and food services sales signals reduced consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Retail sales fall below 380,000 but S&P 500 returns remain positive more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth slows and federal funds rates rise, it indicates economic tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: GDP growth slows and federal funds rates rise, but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, low unemployment signals a strong economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Unemployment is low but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 50% of the time.
